title: CSV files saved from Excel start with a UTF-8 BOM: read them with utf-8-sig
body: Symptom: the first column looks missing (KeyError on the first header, e.g. 'order_id', or rows silently skipped because row.get('sku') is None). Cause: Excel writes a UTF-8 BOM, so with encoding='utf-8' the first header is '\ufefforder_id'. Fix: open with encoding='utf-8-sig' (our vendored vendor/tinycsv.py DEFAULT_ENCODING) - it strips the BOM and still reads plain UTF-8.

title: Flaky order or cache misses across processes: Python str hashes are randomized per process
body: PYTHONHASHSEED is random per process, so set iteration order of strings and hash(str) differ between runs. Symptoms: tests that depend on set order (or Counter.most_common ties fed from a set) fail ~half the time; anything persisted using hash() (cache file names, shard keys) never matches after a restart. Fix: sort explicitly (e.g. key=(-count, name)); use hashlib (sha256) for persistent keys. Reproduce with PYTHONHASHSEED=0..N loops.

title: Money: never use float + round(); use Decimal with ROUND_HALF_UP
body: Finance rounds half-up per line. Python round() is banker's rounding and floats can't represent 2.675 or 1.005, so round(2.675, 2) == 2.67. Use Decimal(str_amount) and .quantize(Decimal('0.01'), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP); keep values Decimal end to end and format with str().

title: bool('false') is True: parse boolean env vars explicitly
body: Config loaders that cast env strings with type(default)(raw) or a {'bool': bool} caster turn 'false', '0', 'no' into True. Parse booleans explicitly: raw.strip().lower() in ('1','true','yes','on'). Applies to NOTIFY_* and INGEST_* style overrides.

title: Python regex: $ matches before a trailing newline; use fullmatch (and ASCII classes)
body: re.match(r'^[a-z]+$', 'bob\n') matches because $ also matches before a final newline. Use re.fullmatch or \Z. Also \w and \d match Unicode letters/digits (é, ٣) unless re.ASCII or an explicit [a-z0-9] class is used.

title: JS: new Date('YYYY-MM-DD') is UTC midnight, not local - dates shift a day in US/NZ
body: Date-only ISO strings are parsed as UTC by new Date() and Date.parse(), while getDate()/startOfDay use local time, so in America/* the date is the previous day and in Pacific/Auckland comparisons are off. Parse calendar dates as local: const [y,m,d]=s.split('-').map(Number); new Date(y, m-1, d). Run tests with TZ=America/Los_Angeles and TZ=Pacific/Auckland.
